added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm (both read null; absent from the manifest and from worker.json and supervisor.json), so the added-failure count was not taken and the field is left as unmeasured rather than zero. A positive control on the same reader shows it does see a failure known to be present: added_failures_from_gate_logs returns (1, ['tests/test_b.py::test_new']) for a head log that adds one FAILED id, (0, []) when both logs are green, and (None, []) when one log is absent. The run's single-arm gate.log ('81 passed', EXIT=0) carries no FAILED or ERROR line, but that comparison is recorded here as prose, not as a count.

findings.text: follow-on: the new confirmation column and its recorded location have no negative control -- the census self-check asserts only three resolve_anchor negatives (missing file, line past end, absent plan section) and never exercises confirmed_by_repair, so a regression that marked every finding confirmed, or dropped the location, would redden nothing and the column's only ground truth is two live rows. Add a fourth control: an identifier absent from the reviewed plan must report (False, '').

follow-on: the negative control that shows the recursive grep reddens runs a replica (negctl_test.py, a hand copy of the assertion body) against the scratch copy rather than the shipped test file, so the red log demonstrates equivalent logic but not the artifact under test. Running tests/test_plan_review_prefix_is_one_constant.py itself against the scratch copy would test the shipped assertion.

follow-on: the §11 evidence block is a live-store snapshot -- the run's own census-determinism.log ends 'EMBEDDED==FRESH False' because a review landed between the embed and the check, while the manifest reads 'currently matches a fresh census run byte for byte'; the reproducibility holds only while the store is stable. A population as-of cutoff (a recorded timestamp filtering the enumerated records) would make the §11 table reproducible rather than a moving target.

justifications.durability: the commit carries a conventional subject and a body stating what changed and why, with no attribution and no plan or ticket identifier; the refactor in review.py/plan_review.py is covered by the gate's store and review tests, and a test asserts plan_review_path's .at-bbbbbbbb sibling is byte-identical through the shared helper. Deducted because the census repairs (the plan-scoped confirmation and its recorded location, and the broad-vs-reader directory cross-check) are verified only by the script's own self-check, which exercises three resolve_anchor negatives and does not exercise confirmed_by_repair at all.
justifications.evidence: gate.log records '81 passed' EXIT=0 at 06d117c6, negative_control.log records '1 failed' EXIT=1, and the census is run-to-run deterministic (RUN1/RUN2 EXIT=0, DIFF EXIT=0); I re-ran census.py at the reviewed head and its table reproduces the committed §11 block byte for byte, and ran a positive control on the added-failure reader (a head log adding one FAILED id returns (1, [that id]), green/green returns 0, a one-sided pair returns None). Deducted because the run's own census-determinism.log ends 'EMBEDDED==FRESH False' while the manifest states the block matches a fresh run byte for byte (true only once the store settled), and because the rglob negative control runs a replica negctl_test.py rather than the shipped test file.
justifications.fit: each mechanism sits with the owner it measures: PLAN_REVIEW_FILE_GLOB is named beside plan_review_path and read by the reader and the census; _blob_suffix is owned by review.py and parameterised by digest length so both keying callers share one rule without moving a stored record. Deducted because plan_review.py reaches into review's private _blob_suffix, and that helper's ValueError message reads 'invalid reviewed_head_sha' even when a plan-review caller passes a bad plan blob.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every one of the six specified repairs landed and is the repair its source review named: PLAN_REVIEW_FILE_GLOB is spelled once at reckon/crew/plan_review.py and read by list_plan_reviews and the census; resolve_anchor loads commit:docs/plans/<slug>.html; confirmed_by_repair is scoped to the reviewed plan_html and returns the enclosing id; the ownership grep is rglob; the PLAN_REVIEW_RUBRICS re-export is gone; review.py:_blob_suffix owns the .at- suffix. I independently reproduced the census output byte for byte; deducted one because the 're-run yields the same two shares as §11' clause was met by rewriting §11 to the grown store's population rather than by holding the shares constant.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff cc80e8ec..06d117c6 touches exactly the reviewed manifest's declared paths, the cumulative landed record was spliced within its §11 section only (11 deletions, other sections untouched), and the reviewed worktree at 06d117c6 is clean.
